text:
ops-bot: ALERT: GPU pool 'us-west-2/gpu-pool-3' saturation >95% for 12m. queue=142, pending_pods=87. admission control starting. dashboard: https://redwood.prod/dashboards/gpu/pool/us-west-2/gpu-pool-3

ashwin: seeing the alert, lots of long-seq jobs. did anyone roll something recently?

maria: I rolled model v2.3.1 to that pool ~10m ago — per-token latency up ~1.3x on our test harness. starting to suspect the model change.

kevin: autoscaler shows zero spare capacity in us-west-2 (AZ a/b). AWS spot quotas also constrained. I'll request emergency capacity but expect ~15m provisioning time.

julia: can we flip stricter admission control and route low-priority work elsewhere? recommend throttling embeddings + large-context generations.

ashwin: applying temp policy 'sre-emergency' to the pool now — max_concurrent_per_pool=80, per_customer_rps=10. patch: 
```yaml
admissionControl:
  pool: us-west-2/gpu-pool-3
  policy: sre-emergency
  maxConcurrent: 80
  perCustomerRPS: 10
```

maria: applied. queue dropped 142 -> 60 in ~2m. :thumbsup:

kevin: still high latencies for >8k token requests. I'll add a routing fallback for smaller generation paths to quantized variants to reduce GPU time.

kevin: running: `rbctl route update --pool us-west-2 --route small-gen --to quant-ggml-2` — routing change initiated.

ashwin: good call. note: adding nodes will hit costs — 12 p4d-like GPUs ~ $35k/mo. mark as emergency spend if we go that route.

maria: created FIN ticket FIN-789 to track cost impact. prefer routing + admission control over immediate heavy scaling.

kevin: requested 8 GPUs in AZ-b as emergency capacity, AWS acknowledged (8 available). ETA ~9m to boot images and register.

ops-bot: INFO: admission control activated; policy=sre-emergency; affected_requests=120; blocked=24

julia: queue now at 28 and falling, latency trending down for most endpoints. Can we lower the alert threshold to 90% to get earlier warning next time? 95% feels tight.

ashwin: agree — lowering alert threshold to 90% gives more runway. filing follow-up ENGOPS-342 to adjust alerts and add 'pending_queue_ratio' metric.

maria: also adding a lightweight quantized catalog entry as an on-call fallback so we don't need ad-hoc routing each incident.

kevin: scale finished, new nodes registered, autoscaler stable. I'll revert admission control back in 10m and drain the temporary nodes after 30m if stable.

ops-bot: RESOLVED: GPU pool 'us-west-2/gpu-pool-3' saturation cleared. duration=28m.

ashwin: thanks all — postmortem notes: model rollout correlated, alert threshold, fallback variant availability, and emergency scaling playbook updates. cc: @maria to own follow-ups.
